title: Zuriel Chapter Introductions — Psalms 1–30
description: Chapter-by-chapter guides to Psalms 1–30, with verse-checked passages and context-sensitive interpretation.

chapters.title: Psalm 1 — The blessed way and two paths
chapters.historicalContext: Psalm 1 belongs to Israel's prayer and worship collection. The opening wisdom psalm contrasts a life rooted in God's instruction with the instability of wickedness.
chapters.overview: Delight in God's instruction is pictured as a tree planted by streams; the contrast is about enduring fruitfulness, not a promise of an effortless life.
chapters.studyObservation: Attend to the psalm's movement, images and speaker. Delight in God's instruction is pictured as a tree planted by streams; the contrast is about enduring fruitfulness, not a promise of an effortless life.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read Psalm 1 as a complete poem, noticing its opening, turning point and conclusion. Compare its theme with the surrounding psalms without assuming every psalm has the same setting.
studyQuestions: What emotion, situation or act of worship shapes this prayer?
Which images or repeated words carry the main message?
How can this psalm shape faithful prayer without turning its poetry into an unconditional promise?
chapters.lifeApplication: Let this psalm form honest prayer, wise action and compassion. The opening wisdom psalm contrasts a life rooted in God's instruction with the instability of wickedness.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: Delight in God's instruction is pictured as a tree planted by streams; the contrast is about enduring fruitfulness, not a promise of an effortless life.
chapters.readingNote: Psalm 1 has 6 verses in the KJV. Read its poetic language in context and distinguish prayer, metaphor, royal imagery and direct instruction.
